tweets: Rameswaram's Ramanathaswamy Temple holds the longest pillared corridor of any Hindu temple in India — granite columns receding nearly 4,000 feet beneath carved ceilings. Tradition holds Rāma consecrated the śivaliṅga here on his return from Laṅkā.

Unique among India's shrines: a Jyotirliṅga sacred to Śaiva worship, yet also one of the four Char Dhām — placing the Rāmāyaṇa's hero at the very heart of Śiva's temple. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history.
